profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Comcast
profile.summary: I enjoy building things and working with new technology. I'm a strong believer in self teaching, sharing knowledge and learning by doing. With a *nix machine, a plain text editor and plenty of coffee great things can happen.

positions.title: Mobile Engineer
positions.description: Android developer on the Xfinity App

positions.title: Build Engineer
positions.description:
- Supporting CI/CD as a service running applications such as Jenkins, SonarQube and Nexus.

- Support/troubleshoot various build/deployment related issues for projects using several languages/frameworks.

- Implemented a disaster recovery solution for our team’s Nexus application that utilized a standby instance running in a second data center that would periodically synced its data with the main Nexus instance. This allowed us to quickly cutover to our standby instance in the event our main Nexus instance was unavailable.

- Implemented monitoring and alerting for our Mac build agents using DataDog, this alerted our team whenever one of our agents went offline or resource utilization exceeded a predefined threshold.

- Setup EC2 elastic build agents for our Jenkins platform. This allowed our system to dynamically provision new build agents in AWS whenever our max build capacity was reached.

positions.title: Senior Automation Engineer
positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States · Remote
positions.description:
-  Work with QA to automate various manual test cases as well as develop tools and documentation to support QA testing efforts across IAS.


- Designed and developed an automation testing framework that would test IAS’s Firewall JS product in a DOMless environment using Python and NodeJs. This brought the QA testing time of DOMless scenarios from 2 days down to 20 minutes.


- Created Jenkins jobs that would execute several suites of automated tests in parallel as a pull-request check for IAS’s Firewall-JS product.


- Created a BrowserStack mobile client library in Python which interacted with BrowserStack’s native app testing service (app uploading, running automated tests, deleting uploaded apps). This provided a convenient mechanism for executing automated test scripts against BrowserStack.


- Created a Puppet manifest for spinning up a Jenkins Docker slave for our CICD team’s Jenkins instance. This allowed their Jenkins instance to run builds within docker containers.


- Operated and administered the QA team’s personal Jenkins instance. Management tasks included scripting a nightly backup process via cron, cleaning up old builds/logs, scheduling nightly execution regression test suites for various projects, etc.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Supporting the continuous delivery process for over 500 projects with a highly skilled and motivated team of four.

- Automating infrastructure provisioning with tools such as Ansible, Test-Kitchen, and ServerSpec.

- Working with my team to develop a new build system to support the CI/CD process for teams across all of Comcast. Making use of Jenkins, Groovy, Jenkins Job DSL, Jenkins Pipeline DSL, Docker, Ansible and much more.

- Providing support for our Gerrit and Github instances, along with facilitating questions on using git, Gerrit and Github.

- Supporting internal artifact repository stores with thousands of artifacts that are utilized to fulfill project dependencies throughout the continuous integration and continuous delivery process.

positions.title: QA Engineer
positions.description:
I worked as a contractor for Comcast Interactive Media in a support role for the QA department. My job was generally supporting the testing effort for all the different teams in several different ways. My work included tasks such as imaging PC laptops and macbook pros in order to maintain a supply of machines for our QA and software engineers to utilize when their main work machines would malfunction. Troubleshooting computer and network issues that hindered the efforts of our engineers. Asset management of mobile testing devices, laptops, desktop computers, monitors, and other computer peripherals. Requesting and provisioning set top boxes to talk to various testing environments so that the engineers could use them in the development and testing of their STB applications.

After expressing interest I eventually transitioned to the automation team and did mobile automated testing for the iOS TV Go app. For automating the tests I utilized the cucumber/calabash testing framework in conjunction with Ruby scripting. Eventually the team transitioned from calabash and switched to using the Appium mobile automation library for testing our mobile apps.

From automation, I transitioned to a newly formed tools team whose primary responsibility was the development and maintainance of various tools that would facilitate the jobs of CIM engineers. While on the tools team I learned Ruby on Rails in order to develop and maintain Cimport, a web portal that hosted some of our tools developed internally.

projects.title: Ansible-role-pypi
projects.description: A role for provisioning a minimal pypi-server

projects.title: YamlBot
projects.description:
A ruby gem that validates yaml files based upon a rules specification.
Systems such as travis-ci, rubocop, and other tools that utilize yaml-based configuration can often present users with a multitude of keys and options that can take on many possible values. Yamlbot allows users to feed it a set of rules, and then validate any yaml file against those rules to ensure correct configuration.
